<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="DjR" /></noinclude><section begin="par114" />{{GHGmargin-letter|114|m}}
3. A further class comprises the very numerous cases, in which the infinitive with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} is used as the object<ref>This view is based upon the fact, that in numerous expressions of this kind (see the examples above) the {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} may be omitted, and the infinitive consequently stand as an actual accusative of the object (see above, ''c''). However, the connexion of the verb with the object is in the latter case closer and more emphatic (hence especially adapted to poetic or prophetic diction), than the looser addition of the infinitive with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}; thus {{GHGheb|text=לֹא אָבוּ שְׁמוֹעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=12}} is equivalent to ''they desired not obeying'' ({{GHGheb|text=לֹא אָבוּ}} also with the infin. abs. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=24}}; cf. {{GHGpar|113|d}}); but {{GHGheb|text=לֹא אָבוּ לִשְׁמֹעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=8}} rather expresses ''they could not make up their mind as to hearkening''. When connected with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, the governing verb has a more independent sense than when it directly governs the accusative of the object.</ref> of a governing verb, hence, again, for ''the direction'' which an action takes. The verbs (or conjugations) which occur most frequently in this combination with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} and an infinitive are: {{GHGheb|text=הֵחֵל}} (with an infinitive without {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=25}}, 31, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=7}}), {{GHGheb|text=הוֹאִיל|translate=to begin}}, {{GHGheb|text=הוֹסִיף}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָסַף}} (prop. ''to add'') ''to continue'', very frequently, even in prose, with an infinitive without {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, 12, 37:5, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=1}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=חָדַל|translate=to cease from, to desist}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּלָּה|translate=to complete, to make an end of}}; {{GHGheb|text=תָּמַם|translate=to be finished}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִקְרִיב|translate=to come near to}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִהֵר|translate=to hasten}} (with an infinitive without {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=18}}); {{GHGheb|text=אָבָה|translate=to be willing}} (with an infinitive without {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=39|verse=9}}); {{GHGheb|text=חָפֵץ|translate=to will, to desire}}; {{GHGheb|text=מֵאֵן|translate=to refuse}} (''to be unwilling''); {{GHGheb|text=בִּקֵּשׁ|translate=to seek}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָכֹל|translate=to be able}} (with an infinitive without {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=50}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=38}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=2}}); {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן}} with an accusative of the person in the sense of ''to give up to some one, to cause'', or ''permit'' him to do something, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=11}} (with an infinitive abs. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=18}}, see {{GHGpar|113|d}}), {{GHGheb|text=יָדַע|translate=to understand}} how to do something (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֲתִידִם עֹרֵר}} is analogous); {{GHGheb|text=לָמַד|translate=to learn}}; {{GHGheb|text=קִוָּה|translate=to wait, expect}} (with a change of subject, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=2}} ''and he waited for it to bring forth grapes'').

{{GHGmargin-letter|114|n}}
We must further mention here a number of verbs in Hiphʿîl (partly denominatives), which express an action in some definite direction (cf. {{GHGpar|53|f}}), as {{GHGheb|text=הִגְדִּיל|translate=to do greatly}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁפִּיל|translate=to make}} (it) ''low'', {{GHGheb|text=הִגְבִּיהַּ|translate=to make}} (it) ''high'', {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽעֱמִיק|translate=to make}} (it) ''deep'', {{GHGheb|text=הִרְחִיק|translate=to make}} (it) ''far, distant'', {{GHGheb|text=הֵיטִיב|translate=to make}} (it) ''good'' (with an infinitive without {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=33|verse=3}}, but {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=17}}, in the same combination, with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}); {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁכִּים|translate=to do}} anything ''early'' ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=127|verse=2}}, along with its opposite {{GHGheb|text=אֵחַר|translate=to do}} something ''late'', with an infinitive without {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}); {{GHGheb|text=הִרְבָּה|translate=to make}} (it) ''much'', {{GHGheb|text=הִפְלָא|translate=to make}} (it) ''wonderful'' (even with a passive infinitive {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=26|verse=15}}),<ref>In almost all these examples the principal idea is properly contained in the infinitive, whilst the governing verb strictly speaking contains only a subordinate adverbial statement, and is therefore best rendered in English by an adverb; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=20}} ''how is it that thou hast found it so quickly?'' (prop. how thou hast hastened to find!), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=27}} ''wherefore didst thou flee secretly?'' So frequently with {{GHGheb|text=הִרְבָּה}} (= ''often, abundantly''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=36|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=21|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=55|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=4|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=38}}, &c.; with {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּב}} (= ''again''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=30|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=11|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=9|verse=14}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=1|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jn|chapter=4|verse=2}}, and the analogous instances in {{GHGpar|120|g}}; also {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=2|verse=1}} ''thou hast asked a hard thing''.</ref> &c.
